is this commented code is not needed. please remove,

I feel like the network parameter should be ordered-before the eid parameter.

I don't think this abstraction is quite right, but we also don't really care for the RBT transport at the moment, and we can use `MCTP_NET_ANY` for the demux daemon (though as it stands, the implementation will yield `-ENOTSUP`)
mmm. I'll give it one check to see if i can improve it.

Given the `fqe` APIs are in the testing set in libpldm and are therefore not exposed in the stable library ABI, I expect CI is not compiling with `PLDM_TRANSPORT_WITH_AF_MCTP` defined, given it's passing.

I see. Is there a way I can make CI compile with `abi-development` mode to test or I shouldn't have to worry about it?
I didn't catch it while testing my latest patch because I was building on `abi-development` mode.

> Is there a way I can make CI compile with abi-development

This is not allowed, as it dissolves the purpose of the testing set in libpldm. The purpose of the testing set is it allows the libpldm maintainers to merge changes adding new APIs for experimentation, without binding the maintainers to supporting those APIs forever as soon as they're merged.


CI is configured so it _doesn't_ build against the testing set so we can change those APIs freely in the knowledge that no applications are using them, because they can't be referenced by any code already merged.

> I shouldn't have to worry about it?

You do have to worry about it - you need to propose a change to libpldm that marks them as stable. Please have a read through the following:

- https://github.com/openbmc/libpldm/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md#library-background
- https://github.com/openbmc/libpldm/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md#stabilising-an-existing-api
I see. I will work on that first then thanks.

I have pushed a PR on libpldm to stabilize those APIs.
